title: Thin Plugin Proto Pad: frictionless LLM extension idea
body:
Purpose / one-liner:
A tiny, developer-friendly plugin format that lets third-party UIs or customer apps run lightweight pre/post-processing locally (or in a sandbox) and call Redwood for the heavy LLM inference — giving fast UX, lower token spend for some flows, and an official distribution surface for vetted integrations.

Context / motivation (notes to self):
- Many customers want to inject local data transformations and UI hooks (e.g., clipboard parsing, local PKCE auth, sensitive redaction) without shipping a full private deployment.
- Current options: integrate on server (adds latency, data egress), run a full Private deployment (heavy), or call Redwood and try to glue client tooling (ad hoc).
- A thin plugin model could: reduce round trips, allow richer client-side UX (autocomplete, instant validation), provide a secure sandbox for small processors, and simplify partner integrations.

What is a "thin plugin" (high level):
- Small JS/WASM bundle (<200KB ideally) that runs in-browser or in a small serverless shim.
- Exposes hooks: prePrompt(input) -> prompt, postResponse(response) -> post-processed
